claims.statement: The ~15s is 252 child-process invocations: instrumenting spawnSync across a real npm test run measured 34.3s of blocking time inside them, against ~34.5s of total suite CPU — the test bodies, assertions and the node --test harness are noise at this scale.

Those 252 spawns come from 5 of 59 files; the 51 files that spawn nothing cost 7.4s serial in total, and 59 empty test files run in 0.36s, so node --test's per-file worker overhead is about 2% and is not where the time goes.

About 12.0s of the 34.3s spent in children is interpreter startup plus doflow's require graph, paid 252 times at a measured 47.5ms floor before any work begins; the rest is real installs materializing ~204 files at 218ms each.

Wall time is floor-limited by one file rather than by total work: node --test parallelizes across files but not within one, so cli-e2e.test.js's 91 spawns and 14.5s of blocked time set the 15.8s suite floor while the other 19.8s of child work runs alongside it on 10 cores.
